topics.label: Lecture introduction and framing
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the opening framing, setting expectations and introducing the topic of complement before substantive teaching begins.

topics.label: Overview and fundamental principles of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the basic nature of complement proteins, the naming conventions, and the pivotal role of component C3.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the three upstream recognition pathways that generate convertases to reach the complement activation threshold.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the primary immune outcomes triggered by activated complement, including opsonization, inflammation, and cell lysis.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: It examines the regulatory proteins that protect host cells from accidental complement activation and damage.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: It details how deficiencies in specific complement components result in distinct clinical vulnerabilities and disease presentations.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: It explores the mechanisms pathogens employ to evade and suppress complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the closing framing to wrap up the lecture and preview the next topic in the course.
